# 05 — Ranges and Character Classes (`melody_cli 0.20.0`)

Black-box findings for: range expressions (`a to z`), `either { ... }` blocks, negation
via `not`, and how literals/symbols are emitted inside these constructs.

All probes: `printf '%s' '<input>' | /workspace/executable` (or file arg). Unless noted,
exit code 0 and output goes to stdout with exactly one trailing `\n`.

---

## 1. Headline semantics (read first)

- **`either { ... }` is ALTERNATION, not a character class.** Items are joined with `|`
  inside a non-capturing group: `either { "a"; "b"; }` → `(?:a|b)`. There is **no**
  merging of items into a class: `either { a to z; <digit>; "_"; }` → `(?:[a-z]|\d|_)`,
  NOT `[a-z0-9_]`.
- **Ranges are bare, unquoted single chars**: `a to z;` → `[a-z]`. Quoted/backticked
  endpoints are a parse error.
- **Range endpoints are emitted completely raw** — no escaping, no validation
  (reversed, identical, `\`, `]`, `^`, `-` all pass through).
- **Real character classes are only produced by**: ranges (`[a-z]`), negated ranges
  (`not a to z;` → `[^a-z]`), negated/class-like symbols (`<alphabetic>` → `[a-zA-Z]`,
  `not <space>;` → `[^ ]`).
- **Keywords are case-sensitive** (`Either`, `TO`, `Not` all fail).

---

## 2. Range expressions

### 2.1 Syntax

- Form: `<char> to <char>` where each endpoint is exactly **one bare printable ASCII
  char** (0x21–0x7E) **or DEL (0x7F)**. No quotes, no backticks, no symbols, no
  escapes, no multi-byte/unicode chars, no space/tab/newline as endpoints.
- Whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines, CRLF, `/* */` comments) is allowed **and
  optional** around `to` and around the endpoints:
  - `a to z;`, `a   to   z;`, `a\nto\nz;`, `a\ttoz;` → `[a-z]`
  - `atoz;` → `[a-z]`, `atoz ;` → `[a-z]`, `ato z;` → `[a-z]` (whitespace fully optional!)
  - `a /* c */ to /* c */ z;` → `[a-z]`
- A trailing `;` is mandatory at statement level: `a to z` (no `;`) → parse error
  (`expected root`, see §8). Leading whitespace before a statement is fine.
- Multi-char endpoints fail: `ab to cd;` → parse error at 1:1 `expected root`.
- Quoted endpoints fail: `"a" to "z";`, `'a' to 'z';`, `` `a` to `z` ``, `'a' to "z";`
  → all parse error at 1:1 `expected root`.
- Unicode endpoints fail: `α to ω;`, `😀 to 😃;` → parse error at 1:1 `expected root`.
- Symbols as endpoints fail: `<digit> to z;`, `<digit> to <char>;` → `expected root`.
- Escape-sequence endpoints fail: `"\n" to "z"` is not a range (parse error).

### 2.2 Emission

`X to Y` → `[X-Y]`, endpoints **verbatim, never escaped**. Full printable-ASCII sweep
(0x21–0x7E) as both start and end endpoint: **all accepted, all emitted raw**, e.g.:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `0 to 9;` | `[0-9]` |
| `a to z;` | `[a-z]` |
| `A to Z;` | `[A-Z]` |
| `! to /;` | `[!-/]` |
| `: to @;` | `[:-@]` |
| `[ to \`;` | `` [[-`] `` |
| `a to ];` | `[a-]]` |
| `] to z;` | `[]-z]` |
| `a to ^;` | `[a-^]` |
| `^ to z;` | `[^-z]` |
| `a to -;` | `[a--]` |
| `- to z;` | `[--z]` |
| `a to \;` | `[a-\]` |
| `\ to a;` | `[\-a]` |
| `{ to };` | `[{-}]` |
| `< to >;` | `[<->]` |
| `a to ";` | `[a-"]` |
| `a to ';` | `[a-']` |
| `; to z;` | `[;-z]` |
| `a to ;;` | `[a-;]` |
| `a to <DEL>;` (0x7F) | `[a-\x7f]` |

### 2.3 No validation

- Reversed: `9 to 0;` → `[9-0]` (exit 0; would be a runtime error in JS, compiler doesn't care)
- Same char: `a to a;` → `[a-a]`
- Mixed case: `a to Z;` → `[a-Z]`

### 2.4 Quantifiers and groups attach directly

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `some of a to z;` | `[a-z]+` |
| `5 of a to z;` | `[a-z]{5}` |
| `option of a to z;` | `[a-z]?` |
| `capture { a to z; }` | `([a-z])` |
| `a to z; 0 to 9;` | `[a-z][0-9]` |

---

## 3. `not` — negated classes

Grammar-wise `not` accepts only: a **range**, a **symbol** (`<...>`), or (per error
messages) an "amount"/"assertion_type" combo — amounts after `not` always end in parse
errors (`not 5 of "a";` → `expected assertion_type`; `not 5 of <boundary>;` → same).
`not` does NOT accept literals, raw, `either`, groups, or another `not`.

| Input | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `not a to z;` | `[^a-z]` | negated class |
| `not 9 to 0;` | `[^9-0]` | reversed still fine |
| `not ! to /;` | `[^!-/]` | endpoints raw |
| `not a to ^;` | `[^a-^]` | `^` endpoint raw even in negated class |
| `notatoz;` | `[^a-z]` | whitespace optional after `not` too |
| `not <digit>;` | `\D` | shorthand negation |
| `not <word>;` | `\W` | |
| `not <boundary>;` | `\B` | |
| `not <space>;` | `[^ ]` | **literal space inside class** |
| `not <newline>;` | `[^\n]` | 2 chars `\`+`n` |
| `not <tab>;` | `[^\t]` | |
| `not <return>;` | `[^\r]` | |
| `not <feed>;` | `[^\f]` | |
| `not <null>;` | `[^\0]` | |
| `not <backspace>;` | `[^\b]` | |
| `not <vertical>;` | `[^\v]` | |
| `not <alphabetic>;` | `[^a-zA-Z]` | |
| `not <alphanumeric>;` | `[^a-zA-Z0-9]` | |
| `not <char>;` | — | **semantic error**: `Error: negative char not allowed` (stderr, exit 65) |
| `not <any>;` | — | `Error: usage of an unrecognized symbol` (stderr, exit 65) — `<any>` doesn't exist |
| `not "a";` | — | parse error 1:5, `expected amount, class_content, or assertion_type` |
| `not `a`;` | — | same parse error |
| `not either { "a"; }` | — | parse error 1:5, `expected amount or assertion_type` |
| `not not <digit>;` | — | parse error 1:5, `expected amount or assertion_type` |

Quantifiers attach: `some of not a to z;` → `[^a-z]+`, `some of not <digit>;` → `\D+`,
`capture { not 0 to 9; }` → `([^0-9])`.

Note: only ONE item can be negated at a time — there is no multi-item negated class
syntax. To combine negations you must alternate them: `either { not <space>; not <digit>; }`
→ `(?:[^ ]|\D)`.

---

## 4. Symbol emission table (context: plain / in `either` / with `not`)

| Symbol | Plain | `not <sym>` |
|---|---|---|
| `<digit>` | `\d` | `\D` |
| `<word>` | `\w` | `\W` |
| `<boundary>` | `\b` | `\B` |
| `<space>` | ` ` (literal space) | `[^ ]` |
| `<newline>` | `\n` (2 chars) | `[^\n]` |
| `<tab>` | `\t` | `[^\t]` |
| `<return>` | `\r` | `[^\r]` |
| `<feed>` | `\f` | `[^\f]` |
| `<null>` | `\0` | `[^\0]` |
| `<backspace>` | `[\b]` | `[^\b]` |
| `<vertical>` | `\v` | `[^\v]` |
| `<alphabetic>` | `[a-zA-Z]` | `[^a-zA-Z]` |
| `<alphanumeric>` | `[a-zA-Z0-9]` | `[^a-zA-Z0-9]` |
| `<char>` | `.` | error `negative char not allowed` |
| `<any>`, `<unicode>`, `<letter>`, `<word boundary>` | — | error `usage of an unrecognized symbol` |

Inside `either`, symbols emit exactly their plain form as one alternative:
`either { <newline>; "a"; }` → `(?:\n|a)`; `either { <space>; "a"; }` → `(?: |a)`;
`either { <alphabetic>; "a"; }` → `(?:[a-zA-Z]|a)`; `either { <char>; "a"; }` → `(?:.|a)`.

---

## 5. `either { ... }` — alternation

### 5.1 Emission rules

- `(?:item1|item2|...)` — always a non-capturing group, even for ONE item:
  `either { "a"; }` → `(?:a)`; `either { a to z; }` → `(?:[a-z])`;
  `either { "ab"; }` → `(?:ab)`.
- Order preserved, duplicates kept: `either { "z"; "a"; }` → `(?:z|a)`;
  `either { "a"; "a"; }` → `(?:a|a)`; `either { a to z; a to z; }` → `(?:[a-z]|[a-z])`.
- No class merging / no factoring, ever.
- Item separators: expression items (literal, raw, range, symbol, `not`, quantified
  expr) must be terminated by `;`. Block items (nested `either {..}`, `capture {..}`)
  must NOT be followed by `;` inside the block:
  - `either { either { "a"; } "b"; }` → `(?:(?:a)|b)`
  - `either { either { "a"; }; "b"; }` → parse error at the `;` (col of `;`),
    `expected literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation`
  - `either { capture { "a"; } "b"; }` → `(?:(a)|b)`
- Whitespace/comments optional everywhere: `either{"a";"b";}` → `(?:a|b)`.
- Items may be quantified: `either { 2 of "a"; "b"; }` → `(?:a{2}|b)`;
  `either { some of "a"; "b"; }` → `(?:a+|b)`.

### 5.2 Quantifiers on `either`

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `some of either { "a"; "b"; }` | `(?:a|b)+` |
| `2 of either { "a"; "b"; }` | `(?:a|b){2}` |
| `lazy some of either { "a"; "b"; }` | `(?:a|b)+?` |
| `some of either { a to z; }` | `(?:[a-z])+` |

### 5.3 `either` errors

| Input | Error (stderr, exit 65) |
|---|---|
| `either { }` | 1:10 `expected literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation` |
| `either { "a" }` (missing `;`) | 1:10 `expected quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, or variable_declaration` |
| `either { "a";; "b"; }` | 1:14 (at 2nd `;`) same long expected-list as empty |
| `either "a"; "b";` (no braces) | 1:8 `expected block` |

### 5.4 Statement concatenation

`either { "a"; } either { "b"; }` → `(?:a)(?:b)`; `0 to 9; either { a to z; }` → `[0-9](?:[a-z])`.

---

## 6. Literal emission & escaping (as observed inside `either` and standalone)

### 6.1 Escaping on emission

Only these chars are backslash-escaped when a literal is emitted:
`.` `+` `*` `?` `(` `)` `[` `]` `{` `}` `^` `$` `|` and `\` (as `\\`).
Everything else (`/ - < > = ! : ; , @ # % & ~ _ \`` space, quotes, unicode) is raw.

Full ASCII punctuation sweep, `either { "<c>"; }`:

- Escaped: `(?:\.)` `(?:\+)` `(?:\*)` `(?:\?)` `(?:\()` `(?:\))` `(?:\[)` `(?:\])`
  `(?:\{)` `(?:\})` `(?:\^)` `(?:\$)` `(?:\|)`
- Raw: `(?:/)` `(?:-)` `(?:<)` `(?:>)` `(?:=)` `(?:!)` `(?::)` `(?:;)` `(?:,)` `(?:@)`
  `(?:#)` `(?:%)` `(?:&)` `(?:~)` `(?:_)` `` (?:`) ``

Standalone literals follow the same rule: `".";` → `\.`, `"a.c*";` → `a\.c\*`
(same for single-quoted).

### 6.2 Escape sequences INSIDE literals (source-level)

Recognized: `\\`, `\"` (double-quoted only), `\'` (single-quoted only), `\/`,
`\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\0`, `\b`, `\f`.

Decoding behavior (verified with `od -c`):

| Source (inside `"..."`) | Emitted bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `\n` | `0x0A` | decoded to a REAL newline byte embedded in the output regex |
| `\t` | `0x09` | real tab byte |
| `\r` | `0x0D` | real CR byte |
| `\0` | `0x00` | real NUL byte |
| `\b` | `0x08` | real backspace byte |
| `\f` | `0x0C` | real form-feed byte |
| `\"` | `"` | decoded quote |
| `\'` | `'` | decoded quote (single-quoted literal) |
| `\\` | `\\` (2 chars) | decoded to `\`, then re-escaped on emission |
| `\/` | `\/` (2 chars) | **NOT decoded** — passes through verbatim (unlike `/` alone → `/`) |

Rejected escapes (parse error at the literal, long expected-list):
`\x41`, `\xff`, `\u0041`, `\u{...}`, `\v`, `\a`, `\q`, `\-`, `` \` ``,
`\'` inside `"..."`, `\"` inside `'...'`.

Note: contrast with symbols — `<newline>` emits the 2-char sequence `\n`, but the
literal `"\n"` emits a raw 0x0A byte.

### 6.3 Raw (backtick) strings

Emitted 100% verbatim, no escaping: `` `a.c*e` `` → `a.c*e`, `` `[a-z]` `` → `[a-z]`,
`` `(a|b)` `` → `(a|b)`, `` `a b` `` → `a b` (spaces OK).
Backslash is NOT allowed inside raw: `` `\d` `` / `` `\d+` `` → parse error.

---

## 7. Comments & whitespace

- Only `/* ... */` block comments; allowed between any tokens (even inside a range:
  `a /* c */ to z;`). Non-nesting: `/* a /* b */ "x";` → `x` (comment ends at first `*/`).
- `//` line comments NOT supported: parse error at the `/`.
- Unterminated comment `/* abc` → parse error 1:1 `expected root`.
- Empty program (`` or only comments) → exit 0, prints a single blank line (`\n`).
- CRLF line endings accepted; leading/trailing whitespace around the program accepted.

---

## 8. Errors: format, streams, exit codes

- ALL errors (parse and semantic) go to **stderr**, exit code **65**, stdout empty.
- Success: regex + one trailing `\n` on stdout. With `-o FILE`: file gets the regex
  **without** trailing newline (stdout gets nothing). `-n`/`--no-color`: no observable
  change when piped (no ANSI codes are emitted anyway when not a TTY).
- Parse error shape (pest-style), exact bytes for `printf 'a to z' | executable`:

```
Error:  --> 1:1
  |
1 | a to z
  | ^---
  |
  = expected root
```

i.e. `Error:  --> <line>:<col>\n  |\n<line> | <source line>\n  | <spaces>^---\n  |\n  = expected <list>\n`
("Error: " then TWO spaces before `-->`; no trailing blank line). Multi-line inputs
report the correct line: an error at line 3 col 3 prints `Error:  --> 3:3` and shows
that source line.
- Whole-program failures (bad statement start, missing final `;`, unterminated
  comment) report 1:1 `expected root` regardless of where the real problem is.
- Errors inside `either` report the actual position and this expected-list:
  `expected literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation`
- After a complete item inside `either` (e.g. missing `;`): position of the item and
  `expected quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, or variable_declaration`.
- Trailing garbage after a valid program (`a to z; xx`) → 1:9
  `expected EOI, literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation`.
- Semantic errors (single line, `Error: ` prefix):
  - `Error: negative char not allowed` (`not <char>;`)
  - `Error: usage of an unrecognized symbol` (`<any>;`, `<unicode>;`, `<letter>;`, `<word boundary>;`)

---

## 9. Quick reference cheat-sheet

```
a to z;                     [a-z]
atoz;                       [a-z]            (whitespace optional)
9 to 0;                     [9-0]            (no validation)
a to ];                     [a-]]            (endpoints raw)
not a to z;                 [^a-z]
not <digit>;                \D
not <space>;                [^ ]
<alphabetic>;               [a-zA-Z]
either { "a"; "b"; }        (?:a|b)
either { "a"; }             (?:a)            (single item still grouped)
either { a to z; <digit>; "_"; }   (?:[a-z]|\d|_)   (NO class merging)
either { not a to z; 0 to 9; }     (?:[^a-z]|[0-9])
some of either { "a"; "b"; }       (?:a|b)+
either { either { "a"; } "b"; }    (?:(?:a)|b)      (nested block: no `;` after)
```

# 05 — Ranges and Character Classes (`melody_cli 0.20.0`)

Black-box findings for: range expressions (`a to z`), `either { ... }` blocks, negation
via `not`, and how literals/symbols are emitted inside these constructs.

All probes: `printf '%s' '<input>' | /workspace/executable` (or file arg). Unless noted,
exit code 0 and output goes to stdout with exactly one trailing `\n`.

---

## 1. Headline semantics (read first)

- **`either { ... }` is ALTERNATION, not a character class.** Items are joined with `|`
  inside a non-capturing group: `either { "a"; "b"; }` → `(?:a|b)`. There is **no**
  merging of items into a class: `either { a to z; <digit>; "_"; }` → `(?:[a-z]|\d|_)`,
  NOT `[a-z0-9_]`.
- **Ranges are bare, unquoted single chars**: `a to z;` → `[a-z]`. Quoted/backticked
  endpoints are a parse error.
- **Range endpoints are emitted completely raw** — no escaping, no validation
  (reversed, identical, `\`, `]`, `^`, `-` all pass through).
- **Real character classes are only produced by**: ranges (`[a-z]`), negated ranges
  (`not a to z;` → `[^a-z]`), negated/class-like symbols (`<alphabetic>` → `[a-zA-Z]`,
  `not <space>;` → `[^ ]`).
- **Keywords are case-sensitive** (`Either`, `TO`, `Not` all fail).

---

## 2. Range expressions

### 2.1 Syntax

- Form: `<char> to <char>` where each endpoint is exactly **one bare printable ASCII
  char** (0x21–0x7E) **or DEL (0x7F)**. No quotes, no backticks, no symbols, no
  escapes, no multi-byte/unicode chars, no space/tab/newline as endpoints.
- Whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines, CRLF, `/* */` comments) is allowed **and
  optional** around `to` and around the endpoints:
  - `a to z;`, `a   to   z;`, `a\nto\nz;`, `a\ttoz;` → `[a-z]`
  - `atoz;` → `[a-z]`, `atoz ;` → `[a-z]`, `ato z;` → `[a-z]` (whitespace fully optional!)
  - `a /* c */ to /* c */ z;` → `[a-z]`
- A trailing `;` is mandatory at statement level: `a to z` (no `;`) → parse error
  (`expected root`, see §8). Leading whitespace before a statement is fine.
- Multi-char endpoints fail: `ab to cd;` → parse error at 1:1 `expected root`.
- Quoted endpoints fail: `"a" to "z";`, `'a' to 'z';`, `` `a` to `z` ``, `'a' to "z";`
  → all parse error at 1:1 `expected root`.
- Unicode endpoints fail: `α to ω;`, `😀 to 😃;` → parse error at 1:1 `expected root`.
- Symbols as endpoints fail: `<digit> to z;`, `<digit> to <char>;` → `expected root`.
- Escape-sequence endpoints fail: `"\n" to "z"` is not a range (parse error).

### 2.2 Emission

`X to Y` → `[X-Y]`, endpoints **verbatim, never escaped**. Full printable-ASCII sweep
(0x21–0x7E) as both start and end endpoint: **all accepted, all emitted raw**, e.g.:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `0 to 9;` | `[0-9]` |
| `a to z;` | `[a-z]` |
| `A to Z;` | `[A-Z]` |
| `! to /;` | `[!-/]` |
| `: to @;` | `[:-@]` |
| `[ to \`;` | `` [[-`] `` |
| `a to ];` | `[a-]]` |
| `] to z;` | `[]-z]` |
| `a to ^;` | `[a-^]` |
| `^ to z;` | `[^-z]` |

| `- to z;` | `[--z]` |

| `\ to a;` | `[\-a]` |
| `{ to };` | `[{-}]` |
| `< to >;` | `[<->]` |
| `a to ";` | `[a-"]` |
| `a to ';` | `[a-']` |
| `; to z;` | `[;-z]` |
| `a to ;;` | `[a-;]` |
| `a to <DEL>;` (0x7F) | `[a-\x7f]` |

- Mixed case: `a to Z;` → `[a-Z]`

| `5 of a to z;` | `[a-z]{5}` |
| `option of a to z;` | `[a-z]?` |
| `capture { a to z; }` | `([a-z])` |
| `a to z; 0 to 9;` | `[a-z][0-9]` |

### 5.2 Quantifiers on `either`

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `some of either { "a"; "b"; }` | `(?:a|b)+` |
| `2 of either { "a"; "b"; }` | `(?:a|b){2}` |
| `lazy some of either { "a"; "b"; }` | `(?:a|b)+?` |
| `some of either { a to z; }` | `(?:[a-z])+` |

### 5.3 `either` errors

| Input | Error (stderr, exit 65) |
|---|---|
| `either { }` | 1:10 `expected literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation` |
| `either { "a" }` (missing `;`) | 1:10 `expected quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, or variable_declaration` |
| `either { "a";; "b"; }` | 1:14 (at 2nd `;`) same long expected-list as empty |
| `either "a"; "b";` (no braces) | 1:8 `expected block` |

### 5.4 Statement concatenation

`either { "a"; } either { "b"; }` → `(?:a)(?:b)`; `0 to 9; either { a to z; }` → `[0-9](?:[a-z])`.

---

## 6. Literal emission & escaping (as observed inside `either` and standalone)

### 6.1 Escaping on emission

Only these chars are backslash-escaped when a literal is emitted:
`.` `+` `*` `?` `(` `)` `[` `]` `{` `}` `^` `$` `|` and `\` (as `\\`).
Everything else (`/ - < > = ! : ; , @ # % & ~ _ \`` space, quotes, unicode) is raw.

Full ASCII punctuation sweep, `either { "<c>"; }`:

- Escaped: `(?:\.)` `(?:\+)` `(?:\*)` `(?:\?)` `(?:\()` `(?:\))` `(?:\[)` `(?:\])`
  `(?:\{)` `(?:\})` `(?:\^)` `(?:\$)` `(?:\|)`
- Raw: `(?:/)` `(?:-)` `(?:<)` `(?:>)` `(?:=)` `(?:!)` `(?::)` `(?:;)` `(?:,)` `(?:@)`
  `(?:#)` `(?:%)` `(?:&)` `(?:~)` `(?:_)` `` (?:`) ``

Standalone literals follow the same rule: `".";` → `\.`, `"a.c*";` → `a\.c\*`
(same for single-quoted).

### 6.2 Escape sequences INSIDE literals (source-level)

Recognized: `\\`, `\"` (double-quoted only), `\'` (single-quoted only), `\/`,
`\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\0`, `\b`, `\f`.

Decoding behavior (verified with `od -c`):

| Source (inside `"..."`) | Emitted bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `\n` | `0x0A` | decoded to a REAL newline byte embedded in the output regex |
| `\t` | `0x09` | real tab byte |
| `\r` | `0x0D` | real CR byte |
| `\0` | `0x00` | real NUL byte |
| `\b` | `0x08` | real backspace byte |
| `\f` | `0x0C` | real form-feed byte |
| `\"` | `"` | decoded quote |
| `\'` | `'` | decoded quote (single-quoted literal) |
| `\\` | `\\` (2 chars) | decoded to `\`, then re-escaped on emission |
| `\/` | `\/` (2 chars) | **NOT decoded** — passes through verbatim (unlike `/` alone → `/`) |

Rejected escapes (parse error at the literal, long expected-list):
`\x41`, `\xff`, `\u0041`, `\u{...}`, `\v`, `\a`, `\q`, `\-`, `` \` ``,
`\'` inside `"..."`, `\"` inside `'...'`.

Note: contrast with symbols — `<newline>` emits the 2-char sequence `\n`, but the
literal `"\n"` emits a raw 0x0A byte.

### 6.3 Raw (backtick) strings

Emitted 100% verbatim, no escaping: `` `a.c*e` `` → `a.c*e`, `` `[a-z]` `` → `[a-z]`,
`` `(a|b)` `` → `(a|b)`, `` `a b` `` → `a b` (spaces OK).
Backslash is NOT allowed inside raw: `` `\d` `` / `` `\d+` `` → parse error.

---

## 7. Comments & whitespace

- Only `/* ... */` block comments; allowed between any tokens (even inside a range:
  `a /* c */ to z;`). Non-nesting: `/* a /* b */ "x";` → `x` (comment ends at first `*/`).
- `//` line comments NOT supported: parse error at the `/`.
- Unterminated comment `/* abc` → parse error 1:1 `expected root`.
- Empty program (`` or only comments) → exit 0, prints a single blank line (`\n`).
- CRLF line endings accepted; leading/trailing whitespace around the program accepted.

---

## 8. Errors: format, streams, exit codes

- ALL errors (parse and semantic) go to **stderr**, exit code **65**, stdout empty.
- Success: regex + one trailing `\n` on stdout. With `-o FILE`: file gets the regex
  **without** trailing newline (stdout gets nothing). `-n`/`--no-color`: no observable
  change when piped (no ANSI codes are emitted anyway when not a TTY).
- Parse error shape (pest-style), exact bytes for `printf 'a to z' | executable`:

```
Error:  --> 1:1
  |
1 | a to z
  | ^---
  |
  = expected root
```

i.e. `Error:  --> <line>:<col>\n  |\n<line> | <source line>\n  | <spaces>^---\n  |\n  = expected <list>\n`
("Error: " then TWO spaces before `-->`; no trailing blank line). Multi-line inputs
report the correct line: an error at line 3 col 3 prints `Error:  --> 3:3` and shows
that source line.
- Whole-program failures (bad statement start, missing final `;`, unterminated
  comment) report 1:1 `expected root` regardless of where the real problem is.
- Errors inside `either` report the actual position and this expected-list:
  `expected literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation`
- After a complete item inside `either` (e.g. missing `;`): position of the item and
  `expected quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, or variable_declaration`.
- Trailing garbage after a valid program (`a to z; xx`) → 1:9
  `expected EOI, literal, raw, not, range, quantifier_quantity, group_declaration, assertion_declaration, variable_declaration, or variable_invocation`.
- Semantic errors (single line, `Error: ` prefix):
  - `Error: negative char not allowed` (`not <char>;`)
  - `Error: usage of an unrecognized symbol` (`<any>;`, `<unicode>;`, `<letter>;`, `<word boundary>;`)

---

## 9. Quick reference cheat-sheet

```
a to z;                     [a-z]
atoz;                       [a-z]            (whitespace optional)
9 to 0;                     [9-0]            (no validation)
a to ];                     [a-]]            (endpoints raw)
not a to z;                 [^a-z]
not <digit>;                \D
not <space>;                [^ ]
<alphabetic>;               [a-zA-Z]
either { "a"; "b"; }        (?:a|b)
either { "a"; }             (?:a)            (single item still grouped)
either { a to z; <digit>; "_"; }   (?:[a-z]|\d|_)   (NO class merging)
either { not a to z; 0 to 9; }     (?:[^a-z]|[0-9])
some of either { "a"; "b"; }       (?:a|b)+
either { either { "a"; } "b"; }    (?:(?:a)|b)      (nested block: no `;` after)
```

payload.resultSummary:
Findings written to `/workspace/notes/05-ranges-classes.md`. Key results:

- **`either { ... }` is alternation, not a class.** `either { a to z; <digit>; "_"; }` → `(?:[a-z]|\d|_)` — items are never merged into `[a-z0-9_]`. Even a single item stays grouped: `either { "a"; }` → `(?:a)`.
- **Ranges use bare single chars**: `a to z;` → `[a-z]`. Quoted/backticked/symbol/unicode endpoints are parse errors. Whitespace is fully optional — `atoz;` and even `notatoz;` compile (`[^a-z]`).
- **Zero escaping, zero validation of range endpoints.** Full ASCII sweep (0x21–0x7F) accepted both sides, emitted raw: `a to ];` → `[a-]]`, `a to \;` → `[a-\]`, reversed `9 to 0;` → `[9-0]` (would crash JS at runtime; compiler doesn't care).
- **`not` negates only ranges and symbols**, one item at a time (no multi-item negated class exists). `not <digit>;` → `\D`, but `not <space>;` → `[^ ]` (literal space in class). `not <char>;` → semantic error `negative char not allowed`; `not "a";` / `not either {...}` → parse errors.
- **Symbol table recorded**: `<alphabetic>` → `[a-zA-Z]`, `<backspace>` → `[\b]`, `<space>` → literal space; `<any>`/`<unicode>`/`<letter>` don't exist (`usage of an unrecognized symbol`).

# 15 — Test Mode (`-t` / `--test`, `-f` / `--test-file`)

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (melody_cli 0.20.0). All findings from black-box probing.

## 1. `-t <string>` / `--test <string>` — test against a string

When `-t` is given, the compiled regex is **not printed**. Instead the regex is
executed against the test string and a one-line verdict is printed to **stdout**
(followed by `\n`). Nothing goes to stderr on either verdict.

- Match:    `'<PREFIX>' matched`
- No match: `'<PREFIX>' did not match`
- **Exit code is `0` in BOTH cases.** A non-match is not an error.

`<PREFIX>` is the **test string itself** (NOT the matched portion), possibly
truncated (see §2). Matching is a *search*, not a full-string match:

| Melody source (stdin) | `-t` arg | stdout | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"hello world";` | `hello world` | `'hello worl...' matched` | 0 |
| `"hello world";` | `goodbye` | `'goodbye' did not match` | 0 |
| `"wor";` | `hello world` | `'hello worl...' matched` | 0 |
| `3 of "a";` | `xxaaayy` | `'xxaaayy' matched` | 0 |
| `"a";` | `aba` | `'aba' matched` | 0 |
| `"a";` | `` (empty) | `'' did not match` | 0 |
| `"";` | `` (empty) | `'' matched` | 0 |
| `"";` | `xyz` | `'xyz' matched` | 0 |
| `"A";` | `a` | `'a' did not match` | 0 (case-sensitive) |

Only ONE line is ever printed — multiple matches in the string are not
enumerated (`some of "a";` vs `aaa aaa` → just `'aaa aaa' matched`).

### Special characters in the test string

Printed **verbatim, no escaping/quoting/sanitizing** (single quotes, double
quotes, backslashes, tabs, newlines all appear literally inside the wrapping
single quotes; a newline in the test string produces a literal newline in the
output):

- `-t "it's a"` → `'it's a' matched`
- `-t "$(printf 'line1\nline2')"` →
  ```
  'line1
  line...' did not match
  ```

## 2. Truncation rule (applies to `-t` string only)

- If the test string is **≤ 10 Unicode scalar values (Rust `chars`)**, it is
  shown in full.
- If **> 10 chars**, the first **10 chars** are shown followed by `...`
  (three ASCII dots), then the closing `'`.

| test string | displayed as |
|---|---|
| `abcdefghij` (10) | `'abcdefghij'` |
| `abcdefghijk` (11) | `'abcdefghij...'` |
| `0123456789A` (11) | `'0123456789...'` |
| `日本語のテキストです` (10 CJK) | shown full, no `...` |
| `日本語のテキストですよ` (11 CJK) | first 10 CJK chars + `...` |
| 12×`🙂` | 10 emoji + `...` |
| `abcde◌́fghij` (e + U+0301 combining = 11 scalars) | `'abcde◌́fghi...'` — combining mark counts as its own char; cut can split a grapheme cluster |
| family-emoji ZWJ sequences | cut mid-cluster after 10 scalars (output may end with a dangling partial grapheme) |

Truncation is by **char count, not bytes**, and not grapheme-cluster aware.
The `-f` filename in the verdict is **never truncated** (see §4).

## 3. Regex engine semantics (relevant to what "matches")

Evidence points to a backtracking engine with lookaround support (fancy-regex
style), operating on the string without any flags (no multiline, no
case-insensitive):

- `ahead { "a"; } "a";` (compiles to `(?=a)a`) vs `a` → matched
- `behind { "a"; } "b";` (compiles to `(?<=a)b`) vs `ab` → matched
- `^`/`$` anchor to start/end of the whole haystack only (see §4 tests with
  `<start>`/`<end>`): `$` does NOT match before a trailing newline.

## 4. `-f <file>` / `--test-file <file>` — test against file contents

- The **entire file content** is the haystack, tested as ONE string (newlines
  included; no per-line mode, no line-ending normalization, BOM preserved).
- The verdict line shows the **path exactly as given on the command line**,
  with **no quotes and no truncation**:
  - `-f fruits.txt` → `fruits.txt matched`
  - `-f ./fruits.txt` → `./fruits.txt matched`
  - `-f /tmp/probe15/fruits.txt` → `/tmp/probe15/fruits.txt matched`
  - `-f a_very_long_file_name.txt` → `a_very_long_file_name.txt did not match`
  - `-f "日本語ファイル.txt"` → `日本語ファイル.txt did not match`
  - `-f "file with spaces.txt"` → `file with spaces.txt matched`
- Verdict goes to stdout, exit `0` for both matched / did not match.
- Empty file: `empty.txt did not match` for `"a";`, `empty.txt matched` for `"";`.

Multi-line / anchor probes against `fruits.txt` = `"apple\nbanana\ncherry\n"`:

| Melody source | result | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `"apple"; <newline>; "banana";` (`apple\nbanana`) | matched | spans lines |
| `"banana"; <newline>; "apple";` | did not match | order matters |
| `<start>; "apple";` (`^apple`) | matched | start of file |
| `<start>; "banana";` (`^banana`) | did not match | NO multiline flag |
| `"cherry"; <end>;` (`cherry$`) | did not match | `$` ≠ before trailing `\n` |
| `"cherry"; <newline>; <end>;` (`cherry\n$`) | matched | `$` = absolute end only |
| file `a\r\nb` vs `"a"; <newline>; "b";` (`a\nb`) | did not match | CRLF kept verbatim |
| file starts with UTF-8 BOM vs `^apple` | did not match | BOM kept verbatim |

### `-f` read failures

- Missing file, directory path, or file with invalid UTF-8 content all produce
  the same error on **stderr** (nothing on stdout), **exit code 74**:
  ```
  Error: unable read file at path nonexistent.txt
  ```
  (Note the exact wording: `unable read`, no `to`. Followed by `\n`.)

## 5. Errors and exit codes (summary)

| situation | stream | exit |
|---|---|---|
| match / no match | stdout | `0` |
| Melody compile error (with `-t` or `-f`) | stderr | `65` |
| test file (`-f`) unreadable | stderr | `74` |
| **input** file unreadable (same message text) | stderr | `65` (!) |
| clap argument conflicts / bad usage | stderr | `2` |

Compile error format (pest-style, stderr, exit 65) — example for input `(`:

```
Error:  --> 1:1
  |
1 | (
  | ^---
  |
  = expected root
```

Another observed compile-time error format (non-pest), also exit 65:
`Error: usage of an unrecognized symbol` (e.g. `capture name { "a"; } <name>;`).

Precedence: the melody source is read and compiled **before** the `-f` test
file is read — `printf '(' | executable -f nonexistent.txt` gives the compile
error (65), not the file error.

Empty or whitespace-only melody source compiles to an **empty regex**, which
matches everything: `executable -t "anything" < /dev/null` → `'anything' matched`.

## 6. Flag interactions (clap-level)

All conflicts print `error: ...` + usage to stderr, exit `2`:

- `-t` conflicts with `-f`:
  `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--test-file <test-file>'`
- `-t` conflicts with `-o`:
  `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>'`
  (no output file is created)
- `-f` conflicts with `-o` (same pattern, `--test-file` vs `--output`)
- `-t` conflicts with `-r` (`--repl`); same for `-f` presumably
- `-t` given twice:
  `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used multiple times`
- `-t` value starting with `-`: `-t "-n"` fails with
  `error: a value is required for '--test <test>' but none was supplied`
  (clap does not allow hyphen-leading values); use `--test=-n`, which works.
- `-n` / `--no-color`: no observable effect on test-mode output — verdict lines
  contain **no ANSI codes even on a TTY** (verified via `script` pty, with and
  without `-n`).
- Full conflict usage line example:
  ```
  error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--test-file <test-file>'

  Usage: executable --test <test> [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```

## 7. Input source combinations (all verified working, exit 0)

- `executable -t "apple" in.mdy` (file arg)
- `executable in.mdy -f fruits.txt`
- `printf '"apple";' | executable -t "apple" -` (explicit `-` stdin)
- `executable -t "apple" < /dev/null` (empty source → empty regex → matched)

(Note: when stdin is a TTY and no input file is given, the CLI refuses to run
at all: prints `No input file supplied and no input piped` plus a hint and the
help text — independent of `-t`.)

## 8. Output byte-level facts

- Verdict line ends with a single `\n` (LF; `\r\n` only when a pty translates it).
- Wrapping quotes are ASCII single quotes `'`; ellipsis is exactly `...`.
- No trailing spaces; stdout is empty on every error path.

import sys, os, time, signal, select
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/repl")
from pty2 import open_pty_pair, EXE

# EOF test: close stdin master after banner; watch CPU + exit
stdin_m, stdin_s = open_pty_pair()
out_m, out_s = open_pty_pair()
err_m, err_s = open_pty_pair()
pid = os.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.setsid()
    os.dup2(stdin_s, 0); os.dup2(out_s, 1); os.dup2(err_s, 2)
    os.execve(EXE, [EXE, "-r"], dict(os.environ))
os.close(stdin_s); os.close(out_s); os.close(err_s)
time.sleep(0.8)
os.close(stdin_m)  # EOF on slave
time.sleep(1.5)
done, st = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
if done:
    print("EOF: exited with", os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(st))
else:
    # check cpu
    with open(f"/proc/{pid}/stat") as f:
        parts = f.read().split()
    utime, stime = int(parts[13]), int(parts[14])
    print(f"EOF: still running, cpu jiffies utime={utime} stime={stime}")
    time.sleep(1.0)
    with open(f"/proc/{pid}/stat") as f:
        parts = f.read().split()
    print(f"  1s later: utime={parts[13]} stime={parts[14]}")
    os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL); os.waitpid(pid, 0)
for fd in (out_m, err_m):
    try:
        while True:
            r,_,_ = select.select([fd],[],[],0.1)
            if not r: break
            d = os.read(fd, 65536)
            if not d: break
    except OSError: pass

# Ctrl-C exit code as seen by shell: send SIGINT, report wait status
stdin_m, stdin_s = open_pty_pair()
out_m, out_s = open_pty_pair()

    os.dup2(stdin_s, 0); os.dup2(out_s, 1); os.dup2(err_s, 2)

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Full spec written to `/workspace/notes/15-test-mode.md`. Key findings:

- **Verdict format**: `'STRING' matched` / `'STRING' did not match` on stdout, exactly one line, **exit code 0 for both** — non-match is not an error.
- **Truncation rule**: the displayed string is the *test argument itself* (not the matched portion); if longer than 10 **Unicode scalar values** (Rust `chars`), show first 10 + `...`. Combining marks count separately and cuts can split grapheme clusters. ≤10 chars shown in full.
- **No escaping**: test-string special chars (quotes, tabs, literal newlines) are printed verbatim inside the wrapping single quotes.
- **Matching is a search** (partial match suffices), case-sensitive, single line of output even with multiple matches.
- **`-f` tests the whole file as one string** (no per-line mode, no CRLF normalization, BOM preserved); verdict shows the **path as typed, unquoted, never truncated**. Anchors confirm **no multiline flag**: `^banana` on line 2 fails, `cherry$` before a trailing `\n` fails.
- **Engine supports lookahead and lookbehind** (fancy-regex-style), not just a linear NFA.
- **Exit codes**: compile error → 65 (pest error on stderr); unreadable `-f` file → 74 with the oddly-worded `Error: unable read file at path X`; unreadable *input* file gives the same message but exit **65**; clap conflicts → 2.
- **Conflicts (exit 2)**: `-t` mutually exclusive with `-f`, `-o`, `-r`; `-f` also excludes `-o`; duplicate `-t` rejected; `-t "-n"` fails (clap rejects hyphen-leading values, must use `--test=-n`).
- **Precedence**: melody source is compiled before the `-f` file is read — a compile error masks a missing test file.
- `-n` is a no-op for test mode: verdict lines have no ANSI color even on a TTY.
- Empty/whitespace-only melody source compiles to an empty regex, which matches everything.

# melody_cli 0.20.0 — CLI Argument Parsing (black-box spec)

Binary: `/workspace/executable`. All findings from execution only.
Unless stated otherwise, probes ran with stdout/stderr as pipes (non-tty).

## Exit codes observed

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success (also: test mismatch, REPL exit, invalid `--generate-completions` shell!) |
| 2 | clap argument-parse errors (unknown flag, missing value, conflicts, repeats, invalid UTF-8 argv) |
| 64 | `-r/--repl` used with piped stdin or stdout |
| 65 | compile errors; input-file read errors (not found / directory / invalid UTF-8); stdin read errors |
| 74 | output file write/create errors; `--test-file` read errors |

## --help / -h

`--help` and `-h` are **byte-identical**, exit 0, printed to stdout, exactly:

```
A CLI wrapping the Melody language compiler

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

Arguments:
  [INPUT_FILE_PATH]  Read from a file
                     Use '-' and or pipe input to read from stdin

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>           Write to a file
  -n, --no-color                            Print output with no color
  -r, --repl                                Start the Melody REPL
      --generate-completions <completions>  Outputs completions for the selected shell
                                            To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell
  -t, --test <test>                         Test the compiled regex against a string
  -f, --test-file <test-file>               Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file
  -h, --help                                Print help
  -V, --version                             Print version
```

(trailing newline after last line; note the typo "Use '-' and or pipe input" is verbatim).

Note: usage line says `executable` (argv[0] basename as invoked; completions scripts are generated for the name `melody`).

## --version / -V

stdout: `melody_cli 0.20.0\n`, exit 0. Both forms identical.

## Precedence / short-circuit ordering

clap processes left to right; `--help`/`--version` short-circuit **only if reached before any error**:

- `executable --help --bogus` → full help, exit 0
- `executable --bogus --help` → unknown-argument error, exit 2
- `executable --version --bogus` → `melody_cli 0.20.0`, exit 0
- `executable --bogus --version` → error, exit 2

## Unknown arguments (verbatim)

`executable --bogus` → stderr, exit 2:

```
error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found

  tip: to pass '--bogus' as a value, use '-- --bogus'

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

Same shape for `-x` (`tip: to pass '-x' as a value, use '-- -x'`).

Near-miss long flags get a "similar argument" tip. `executable --out x` → exit 2:

```
error: unexpected argument '--out' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--output'

Usage: executable <INPUT_FILE_PATH|--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>|--no-color|--repl|--generate-completions <completions>|--test <test>|--test-file <test-file>>

For more information, try '--help'.
```

NOTE the **usage line changes** once at least one valid argument was consumed before the error:
- error before any valid arg parsed (`--bogus x`, `--bogus -n`) → `Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]`
- error after a valid arg parsed (`x --bogus`, `-n --bogus`, `--out x` where `x` became the positional) → `Usage: executable <INPUT_FILE_PATH|--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>|--no-color|--repl|--generate-completions <completions>|--test <test>|--test-file <test-file>>`

No long-flag abbreviation is accepted.

## Missing values (verbatim, all exit 2, stderr)

```
error: a value is required for '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>' but none was supplied

For more information, try '--help'.
```

Same template for `--test <test>`, `--test-file <test-file>`, `--generate-completions <completions>` (short and long forms produce the identical message naming the long form). Also triggered when the next token is another flag or `--` (e.g. `-o -n`, `-o -- -x` → same error; flags/`--` are never consumed as values).

## Positional argument

- Zero or one positional `[INPUT_FILE_PATH]`. Two positionals → exit 2:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument 'b.mel' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  (no "tip" line for a plain-word extra positional; a second `-` gives `error: unexpected argument '-' found`).
- `-` as positional = read stdin. `-- -` also reads stdin. `-- -h` → treated as filename `-h` → `Error: unable read file at path -h`, exit 65.
- `--` alone (no positional) → reads stdin normally.
- If both a file arg and piped stdin are present, the **file wins**; stdin ignored.
- Flags may appear after the positional (`executable a.mel -n` works).

## Input source errors

| Case | stderr | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| file not found | `Error: unable read file at path nope.mel\n` | 65 |
| path is a directory (`.`, `/tmp/cli_probe`) | `Error: unable read file at path <path>\n` | 65 |
| invalid UTF-8 **in file** | `Error: unable read file at path <path>\n` (same as not-found!) | 65 |
| invalid UTF-8 **on stdin** (piped or via `-`) | `Error: unable to read stdin\n` | 65 |
| invalid UTF-8 **in an argv value** (e.g. `-t $'\xff'`) | `error: invalid UTF-8 was detected in one or more arguments\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n` | 2 |

Note the input-file message is literally "unable read file" (missing "to") — verbatim.

## Success output (stdout)

- `printf '5 of "a";' | executable` → stdout `a{5}\n`, exit 0 (compiled regex + exactly one `\n`).
- Empty input (empty stdin, empty file) → stdout is just `\n`, exit 0.
- Compile error → stdout empty; stderr (uncolored form):
  ```
  Error:  --> 1:1
    |
  1 | bad !!!
    | ^---
    |
    = expected root
  ```
  exit 65. (Note: `Error:` followed by **two** spaces; pest report embedded; single trailing `\n`.)

## -o / --output

- Writes compiled regex to the file **with NO trailing newline** (`a{5}` = 4 bytes). stdout stays silent. Exit 0.
- Empty input → creates a **0-byte** file, exit 0.
- Truncates/overwrites existing files.
- Compile error → file is **not created**, error to stderr, exit 65.
- `-o` file content is never colorized, even with colors forced.
- `-o -` writes to a file literally named `-` (not stdout).
- `-oatt.txt` (attached) and `-o=eq.txt` (writes `eq.txt`, `=` stripped) and `--output=eq.txt` all work.
- `--output=` (empty value) → `Error: \n` (empty path after "Error: "), exit 74.
- Unwritable target (nonexistent dir, `.`, `/dev/full` write failure) → `Error: <path>\n`, exit 74. Message is just `Error: ` + path, no reason text.

## -t / --test, -f / --test-file

- Compile the input, then test. The compiled regex is **NOT printed**; only the verdict line, exit 0 either way:
  - match: `'<test-string>' matched\n`
  - no match: `'<test-string>' did not match\n`
  - `-f`: `<file-path> matched\n` / `<file-path> did not match\n` (path unquoted, no quotes; test string IS wrapped in single quotes)
- Matching is a **search**, not full match: regex `a{5}` matches `aaaaaa` and `baaaaa`.
- Empty test string allowed: `--test=` → `'' did not match`.
- Test strings starting with `-`: `-t -x` fails (`error: unexpected argument '-x' found` + tip, exit 2), but `-t-x` and `--test=-x` work.
- Compile error → exit 65, verdict not printed.
- `-f` file not found / is a directory / invalid UTF-8 → `Error: unable read file at path <path>\n`, exit **74** (different from input-file's 65!).

## -r / --repl

- With piped stdin OR piped stdout (also `< /dev/null`): stderr `Error: repl argument supplied with piped input or output\n`, exit **64**. Requires both stdin and stdout to be TTYs.
- On a TTY prints banner then a `~ ` prompt (verbatim from pty, `\r\n` shown as newlines):
  ```
  Melody REPL v0.20.0

  Commands:

  - :u, :undo - undo the latest line
  - :r, :redo - redo the latest undo
  - :c, :clear - clear all REPL history and previous input
  - :s, :source - print all previously entered lines
  - :e, :exit - exit the REPL

  ~ 
  ```
- Each entered line is compiled and its regex printed on the next line (e.g. input `5 of "a";` → `a{5}`); compile errors print the pest `Error: ...` block and the REPL continues.
- `:e` or `:exit` prints `exit\n` and exits with code 0.
- EOF on stdin does **not** terminate the REPL (it re-prompts forever).
- `-r -o file`: accepted by clap; on a TTY the REPL starts and `-o` is silently ignored (no file created), exit 0.

## --generate-completions

- Accepted values (case-sensitive): `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `elvish`, `powershell`. Output on stdout, exit 0. Scripts are generated for command name **`melody`** (e.g. bash fn `_melody()`, zsh `#compdef melody`, fish `complete -c melody ...`).
- Any other value → **exit 0** (sic), stdout empty, stderr:
  ```
  Unknown or unsupported shell: 'bogus'
  Try one of: 'bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'elvish', 'powershell'

  ```
  (ends with a blank line, i.e. `...powershell'\n\n`). `Bash`/`BASH` rejected the same way.

## Conflicts and repeats (clap, exit 2, stderr)

Mutually conflicting pairs (message subject = the argument that appeared **first** in argv; usage line names that same first argument):

- `-o` × `-t`, `-o` × `-f`, `-t` × `-f`, `-r` × `-t`, `-r` × `-f`, `-r` × `--generate-completions`, `-o` × `--generate-completions`, `-t` × `--generate-completions`, `--generate-completions` × `[INPUT_FILE_PATH]`
- `--generate-completions` is compatible with `-n` only.
- `-r` × `-o` do NOT conflict (runtime REPL path ignores `-o`).

Template (example `executable -t x -o y`):

```
error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>'

Usage: executable --test <test> [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

Reverse order (`-o y -t x`) → `error: the argument '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>' cannot be used with '--test <test>'` and `Usage: executable --output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH> [INPUT_FILE_PATH]`.

gc × positional: `error: the argument '--generate-completions <completions>' cannot be used with '[INPUT_FILE_PATH]'`.

Repeats are rejected — even boolean flags:
- `-t a -t b` → `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used multiple times` + short usage, exit 2
- `-n -n` → `error: the argument '--no-color' cannot be used multiple times`, exit 2
- `-o x -o y` → `error: the argument '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>' cannot be used multiple times`, exit 2

Short-flag clustering works: `-nt "aaaaa"` = `-n -t aaaaa`; `-tn` = `-t` with value `n` (value-taking flag consumes the rest of the cluster).

## Color behavior (--no-color, env, TTY)

Surprising: colors are essentially NEVER auto-enabled — not on a real TTY (verified via pty with `TERM=xterm-256color`), not with `CLICOLOR=1`, and `NO_COLOR` is ignored entirely. The only thing that enables color:

- `CLICOLOR_FORCE` set to any value **except** `0` — including the empty string — turns colors ON, even when piped. `CLICOLOR_FORCE=0` or unset → off.
- `-n` / `--no-color` forces colors OFF and overrides `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`.

Color escape codes (bright variants), when enabled:

| Output | Bytes |
|---|---|
| compiled regex (stdout) | `\x1b[94m` + regex + `\x1b[0m` + `\n` |
| `-t` match | `'<test>' \x1b[92mmatched\x1b[0m\n` |
| `-t` mismatch | `'<test>' \x1b[91mdid not match\x1b[0m\n` |
| `-f` match/mismatch | `<path> \x1b[92mmatched\x1b[0m\n` / `<path> \x1b[91mdid not match\x1b[0m\n` |
| compile error & all `Error: ...` messages (stderr) | whole message wrapped: `\x1b[91m<message>\x1b[0m\n` (internal newlines of pest report are inside the red span) |
| gc bad shell (stderr) | `\x1b[91mUnknown or unsupported shell: 'bogus'\x1b[0m\n` + `\x1b[94mTry one of: 'bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'elvish', 'powershell'\x1b[0m\n\n` (line 1 red, line 2 blue) |
| clap errors (exit 2) | never colored |
| `-o` file content | never colored |

## Summary of message formats

- Runtime errors: `Error: <msg>\n` on stderr (red span when colored). Exit 64/65/74 per table above.
- clap errors: `error: <msg>\n\n[  tip: ...\n\n]Usage: ...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n` on stderr, exit 2.
- gc bad-shell message: on stderr, exit **0** (bug-compatible behavior worth preserving).

  - :e, :exit - exit the REPL

  ~ 
  ```
- Each entered line is compiled and its regex printed on the next line (e.g. input `5 of "a";` → `a{5}`); compile errors print the pest `Error: ...` block and the REPL continues.

- EOF on stdin does **not** terminate the REPL (it re-prompts forever).
- `-r -o file`: accepted by clap; on a TTY the REPL starts and `-o` is silently ignored (no file created), exit 0.

## --generate-completions

- Accepted values (case-sensitive): `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `elvish`, `powershell`. Output on stdout, exit 0. Scripts are generated for command name **`melody`** (e.g. bash fn `_melody()`, zsh `#compdef melody`, fish `complete -c melody ...`).

  ```
  Unknown or unsupported shell: 'bogus'
  Try one of: 'bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'elvish', 'powershell'

  ```
  (ends with a blank line, i.e. `...powershell'\n\n`). `Bash`/`BASH` rejected the same way.

Mutually conflicting pairs (message subject = the argument that appeared **first** in argv; usage line names that same first argument):

- `-o` × `-t`, `-o` × `-f`, `-t` × `-f`, `-r` × `-t`, `-r` × `-f`, `-r` × `--generate-completions`, `-o` × `--generate-completions`, `-t` × `--generate-completions`, `--generate-completions` × `[INPUT_FILE_PATH]`
- `--generate-completions` is compatible with `-n` only.
- `-r` × `-o` do NOT conflict (runtime REPL path ignores `-o`).

```
error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>'

Usage: executable --test <test> [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

Reverse order (`-o y -t x`) → `error: the argument '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>' cannot be used with '--test <test>'` and `Usage: executable --output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH> [INPUT_FILE_PATH]`.

gc × positional: `error: the argument '--generate-completions <completions>' cannot be used with '[INPUT_FILE_PATH]'`.

- `-t a -t b` → `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used multiple times` + short usage, exit 2
- `-n -n` → `error: the argument '--no-color' cannot be used multiple times`, exit 2
- `-o x -o y` → `error: the argument '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>' cannot be used multiple times`, exit 2

Short-flag clustering works: `-nt "aaaaa"` = `-n -t aaaaa`; `-tn` = `-t` with value `n` (value-taking flag consumes the rest of the cluster).

- `CLICOLOR_FORCE` set to any value **except** `0` — including the empty string — turns colors ON, even when piped. `CLICOLOR_FORCE=0` or unset → off.
- `-n` / `--no-color` forces colors OFF and overrides `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`.

Color escape codes (bright variants), when enabled:

| Output | Bytes |
|---|---|
| compiled regex (stdout) | `\x1b[94m` + regex + `\x1b[0m` + `\n` |
| `-t` match | `'<test>' \x1b[92mmatched\x1b[0m\n` |
| `-t` mismatch | `'<test>' \x1b[91mdid not match\x1b[0m\n` |
| `-f` match/mismatch | `<path> \x1b[92mmatched\x1b[0m\n` / `<path> \x1b[91mdid not match\x1b[0m\n` |
| compile error & all `Error: ...` messages (stderr) | whole message wrapped: `\x1b[91m<message>\x1b[0m\n` (internal newlines of pest report are inside the red span) |
| gc bad shell (stderr) | `\x1b[91mUnknown or unsupported shell: 'bogus'\x1b[0m\n` + `\x1b[94mTry one of: 'bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'elvish', 'powershell'\x1b[0m\n\n` (line 1 red, line 2 blue) |
| clap errors (exit 2) | never colored |
| `-o` file content | never colored |

## Summary of message formats

- Runtime errors: `Error: <msg>\n` on stderr (red span when colored). Exit 64/65/74 per table above.
- clap errors: `error: <msg>\n\n[  tip: ...\n\n]Usage: ...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n` on stderr, exit 2.
- gc bad-shell message: on stderr, exit **0** (bug-compatible behavior worth preserving).

# 16 — TTY and Color Behavior (melody_cli 0.20.0)

Binary: `/workspace/executable`. Probed via `script -qec`, a custom `pty.fork` harness,
and an fd-isolation harness (tty placed on exactly one of stdin/stdout/stderr).
`\x1b` = ESC (0x1b). On a pty, the terminal line discipline rewrites `\n` → `\r\n`
(ONLCR); the binary itself always writes plain `\n`. All byte dumps below show what
the *binary* wrote (pipe captures) unless marked `(pty)` — pty captures show `\r\n`
purely due to the pty.

## HEADLINE FINDING: TTY auto-detection NEVER enables color

- No escape sequences are ever emitted merely because stdout/stderr/stdin is a TTY.
  Verified with: `pty.fork` (all fds on pty), `script -qec`, and tty on exactly one
  fd at a time (in/out/err) with `TERM=xterm`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM=dumb`,
  `COLORTERM=truecolor`. Output is byte-identical to piped output (modulo pty `\r\n`).
- **Color is enabled iff env `CLICOLOR_FORCE` is set to any value except the exact
  string `"0"`** — including `""` (empty), `"false"`, `"00"`, `"1"`, `"true"`, `"2"`.
  It works even when stdout is a pipe/file.
- **`-n` / `--no-color` overrides `CLICOLOR_FORCE`** (flag wins over env).
- **`NO_COLOR` is completely ignored** — `NO_COLOR=1 CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` still colors.
- **`CLICOLOR` is ignored** (`CLICOLOR=1` on a tty → no color; `CLICOLOR=0` with
  `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` → still colors). `TERM` and `FORCE_COLOR` are ignored.
- Effective rule: `color = (CLICOLOR_FORCE present && CLICOLOR_FORCE != "0") && !no_color_flag`.

## Color palette (only 4 codes ever observed)

| Code | Meaning | Used for |
|------|---------|----------|
| `\x1b[94m` … `\x1b[0m` | bright blue | compiled regex on stdout; REPL prompt `~ `; REPL source lines; "no input" stderr msg; "Try one of:" line |
| `\x1b[92m` … `\x1b[0m` | bright green | the word `matched`; REPL banner/headings/command echo words |
| `\x1b[91m` … `\x1b[0m` | bright red | the words `did not match`; entire `Error: …` blocks; REPL `no lines to print` |
| `\x1b[2m` … `\x1b[0m` | dim | line numbers in REPL `:s`/`:source` output |

Colors wrap whole strings: one opening code, content, one `\x1b[0m`. No nesting.

## Successful compile

- Pipe / file / tty (no force): stdout = `<regex>\n`. e.g. `5 of "a";` → `a{5}\n`. Exit 0.
- With color: stdout = `\x1b[94m` + regex + `\x1b[0m\n`. Empty program compiles to an
  empty regex: plain → `\n`; colored → `\x1b[94m\x1b[0m\n`.
- `-o FILE`: writes regex to file **with no trailing newline, never colored**
  (`a{5}`, 4 bytes); stdout is empty; exit 0. Color flag irrelevant to file content.

## Compile errors (pest-style)

- stderr, exit 65. Uncolored by default even on a TTY:

```
Error:  --> 1:1
  |
1 | 5 oops "a";
  | ^---
  |
  = expected root
```

(Note `Error:` + **two** spaces before `-->`; trailing `\n`.)
- With color: the **entire block** (from `Error:` through `expected root`, excluding
  final `\n`) is wrapped in one `\x1b[91m` … `\x1b[0m`, then `\n`.
- Unreadable input file: stderr `Error: unable read file at path nope.mdy\n`
  (sic — no "to"), exit **65**; whole line red when colored. Same message for `-f`
  with a missing test file, but exit **74** then.

## `-t` / `--test` and `-f` / `--test-file`

- stdout, exit **0 for both match and non-match**:
  - match: `'<test>' matched\n`; colored: `'<test>' \x1b[92mmatched\x1b[0m\n`
    (subject + space uncolored; only `matched` green).
  - non-match: `'<test>' did not match\n`; colored: `'<test>' \x1b[91mdid not match\x1b[0m\n`.
- Subject is single-quoted verbatim for `-t`; for `-f` the **file path** (not its
  contents) is printed unquoted: `t.txt matched\n`.
- Compile error with `-t`: normal pest error on stderr, exit 65 (no test output).
- `-t` conflicts with `-o` and with `-r`: clap error, exit 2 (see below).

## REPL (`-r`)

- Requires **both stdin AND stdout to be TTYs**. If either is piped/redirected:
  stderr `Error: repl argument supplied with piped input or output\n`, exit **64**
  (whole line red when colored). stdin from `/dev/null` counts as piped.
- Uncolored session (pty, input `5 of "a";` then `:exit`; `⏎` = `\r\n`, echo omitted):

```
Melody REPL v0.20.0⏎
⏎
Commands:⏎
⏎
- :u, :undo - undo the latest line⏎
- :r, :redo - redo the latest undo⏎
- :c, :clear - clear all REPL history and previous input⏎
- :s, :source - print all previously entered lines⏎
- :e, :exit - exit the REPL⏎
⏎
~ a{5}⏎
⏎
~ exit⏎
```

- Colored session, exact byte stream (pty capture; user input lines shown as `‹…›`
  are tty echo, not program output):

```
\x1b[92mMelody REPL v0.20.0\x1b[0m\r\n
\r\n
\x1b[92mCommands:\x1b[0m\r\n
\r\n
- \x1b[94m:u, :undo\x1b[0m - \x1b[92mundo the latest line\x1b[0m\r\n
- \x1b[94m:r, :redo\x1b[0m - \x1b[92mredo the latest undo\x1b[0m\r\n
- \x1b[94m:c, :clear\x1b[0m - \x1b[92mclear all REPL history and previous input\x1b[0m\r\n
- \x1b[94m:s, :source\x1b[0m - \x1b[92mprint all previously entered lines\x1b[0m\r\n
- \x1b[94m:e, :exit\x1b[0m - \x1b[92mexit the REPL\x1b[0m\r\n
\r\n
\x1b[94m~ \x1b[0m‹5 of "a";›\r\n
\x1b[94ma{5}\x1b[0m\r\n
\r\n
\x1b[94m~ \x1b[0m‹:exit›\r\n
\x1b[92mexit\x1b[0m\r\n
```

- REPL color rules: banner + `Commands:` + command descriptions + the words
  `source`/`undo`/`redo`/`clear`/`exit` echoed after each `:` command → 92 (green).
  Command names in help, prompt `~ `, compiled regex per line, and source lines → 94
  (blue). Errors → whole pest block in 91 (red). `:s` line numbers → `\x1b[2m` (dim),
  e.g. `\x1b[2m1\x1b[0m \x1b[94m5 of "a";\x1b[0m`.
- `:s` with empty history: `\x1b[91mno lines to print\n\x1b[0m\n` (note the newline
  *inside* the red span). After each result a blank line precedes the next prompt.
- A bad line in the REPL prints the pest error (red when colored) and the session
  continues; line numbers in the error are cumulative across entered lines
  (`--> 2:1` for the second line).
- Exiting: `:exit`/`:e` prints `exit` (green when colored), exit code 0.
  **Ctrl-D does NOT exit** (prints blank line, re-prompts). Ctrl-C kills the process
  via default SIGINT (no cleanup message; shell sees signal 2 / exit 130).
- `-r` accepts an `[INPUT_FILE_PATH]` argument but does **not** load it (`:s` shows
  `no lines to print`).
- `-n` on REPL: all color suppressed even with `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`.

## Help, version, completions, clap errors — never colored

- `-h`/`--help`: plain text on stdout, exit 0, **no color even with
  `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` and TTY**. Usage line uses argv[0] basename:
  `Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]`.
- `-V`/`--version`: `melody_cli 0.20.0\n` on stdout, exit 0, never colored.
- `--generate-completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell>`: plain clap_complete
  script on stdout, never colored.
- Unknown shell, e.g. `--generate-completions fishy`: **exit 0(!)**, stdout empty,
  stderr:
  ```
  Unknown or unsupported shell: 'fishy'
  Try one of: 'bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'elvish', 'powershell'
  ```
  plus a trailing blank line. Colored: line 1 in `\x1b[91m…\x1b[0m`, line 2 in
  `\x1b[94m…\x1b[0m`.
- clap usage errors (unknown flag, `-t`+`-o` conflict, etc.): plain text on stderr,
  exit **2**, never colored (clap compiled without color). E.g.:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--nope' found

    tip: to pass '--nope' as a value, use '-- --nope'

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Conflict form: `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>'`
  with `Usage: executable --test <test> <INPUT_FILE_PATH>`.

## No-input case (stdin is a TTY, no file arg)

- If stdin is a TTY and no input file given: the binary does **not** read stdin.
  - stderr:
    ```
    No input file supplied and no input piped
    Try adding a path argument: 'melody ./file.mdy'
    ```
    (both lines wrapped together in `\x1b[94m…\x1b[0m` when colored — blue, not red!)
  - stdout: a blank line followed by a **hardcoded** full help text (never colored)
    whose usage line says `Usage: melody_cli [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]` — note the
    hardcoded `melody_cli` vs clap's argv[0]-based `executable` in real `-h` output.
  - exit code **66**.

## Misc

- `-` as input path reads piped stdin, same coloring as file input.
- Reading empty piped stdin with no args compiles the empty program: `\n`
  (colored: `\x1b[94m\x1b[0m\n`), exit 0.
- Exit codes observed: 0 success (incl. `-t` non-match, unknown-shell); 2 clap
  usage error; 64 REPL with piped in/out; 65 compile error / unreadable input file;
  66 no input on TTY stdin; 74 unreadable `-f` test file.

    tip: to pass '--nope' as a value, use '-- --nope'

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Conflict form: `error: the argument '--test <test>' cannot be used with '--output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>'`
  with `Usage: executable --test <test> <INPUT_FILE_PATH>`.

## No-input case (stdin is a TTY, no file arg)

- If stdin is a TTY and no input file given: the binary does **not** read stdin.
  - stderr:
    ```
    No input file supplied and no input piped
    Try adding a path argument: 'melody ./file.mdy'
    ```
    (both lines wrapped together in `\x1b[94m…\x1b[0m` when colored — blue, not red!)
  - stdout: a blank line followed by a **hardcoded** full help text (never colored)
    whose usage line says `Usage: melody_cli [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]` — note the
    hardcoded `melody_cli` vs clap's argv[0]-based `executable` in real `-h` output.
  - exit code **66**.

## Misc

- `-` as input path reads piped stdin, same coloring as file input.
- Reading empty piped stdin with no args compiles the empty program: `\n`
  (colored: `\x1b[94m\x1b[0m\n`), exit 0.
- Exit codes observed: 0 success (incl. `-t` non-match, unknown-shell); 2 clap
  usage error; 64 REPL with piped in/out; 65 compile error / unreadable input file;
  66 no input on TTY stdin; 74 unreadable `-f` test file.

Full spec written to `/workspace/notes/12-cli.md`. Key findings: - **Exit-code map**: 0 success, 2 clap errors, 64 repl-with-piped-io, 65 compile + input-file/stdin read errors, 74 output-write + `--test-file` read errors. Note the input-file vs test-file split (65 vs 74) for the identical message `Error: unable read file at path

` (typo "unable read" is verbatim). - **`-o` quirks**: writes regex with **no trailing newline**, stdout silent, exit 0; empty input → 0-byte file; compile error → file not created; write failure → `Error: ` (no reason), exit 74; `-o -` writes a file literally named `-`. - **`--generate-completions bogus` exits 0** with the error on stderr ending in a blank line; valid shells are bash/zsh/fish/elvish/powershell, case-sensitive, generated for command name `melody` (not `executable`). - **Invalid UTF-8**: in input file → same "unable read file" as not-found (65); on stdin → `Error: unable to read stdin` (65); in argv → clap error (2). - **Colors are never auto-enabled** — not on a real TTY, not with `CLICOLOR=1`; `NO_COLOR` ignored. Only `CLICOLOR_FORCE` set to anything except `0` (even empty) turns them on; `-n` overrides even that. Codes: regex `\x1b[94m`, matched `\x1b[92m`, errors/mismatch `\x1b[91m`. - **Help/version short-circuit is order-dependent**: `--help --bogus` prints help (0), `--bogus --help` errors (2). Usage line also changes to a long `` alternation form if any valid arg was parsed before the error. - **Conflicts**: subject of "cannot be used with" = first arg in argv order; even boolean flags reject repeats (`-n -n` → exit 2). - **`-t`/`-f`**: print only `'str' matched` / ` did not match` (search semantics, not full match), exit 0 either way; compiled regex not printed. - **REPL**: requires TTY on both stdin and stdout else exit 64; banner `Melody REPL v0.20.0` + 5 colon-commands, prompt `~ `, `:e`/`:exit` print `exit` and quit 0; EOF does not terminate it; `-r -o` silently ignores `-o`.

payload.resultSummary:
Findings written to `/workspace/notes/03-quantifiers.md`. Key results:

- **Six quantifier forms only**: `N of` → `{N}`, `N to M of` → `{N,M}`, `some`/`any`/`option of` → `+`/`*`/`?`, `over N of` → `{N+1,}`. `lazy` is a prefix on any of them, appending `?`. Everything else (`at least`, `between`, `up to`, `exactly`, …) is unrecognized; keywords are case-sensitive.
- **Three different number code paths** (the big surprise): `N of` copies digits verbatim with zero validation (`05 of`, `999999999999999999999 of` pass through); `N to M of` parses both as u64 only to validate `N<=M` but still emits the original strings (`3 to 03` → `{3,03}`, N>M or >u64::MAX → `Error: usage of an invalid quantifier range`); `over N of` parses u64 and adds 1 (`over 05` → `{6,}`; overflow at u64::MAX → `Error: could not parse an amount`).
- **Grouping rule**: single-char compiled atoms stay bare (`a{2}`, `\.{2}`, `😀{2}` — counted in chars, not bytes); anything longer is wrapped `(?:ab){2}`. `either`/`capture`/`match` blocks keep their own group syntax (`(?:a|b){2}`, `(a)+`, `(?<name>ab){2}`).
- **Quantifiable targets**: literals (single or double quotes), backtick raw strings (unescaped, `(?:a+){2}`), most symbols, `not <symbol>` (`\D{2}`, `\B{2}`). `<boundary>` is quantifiable → `\b{2}` (semantically odd but verbatim). `<start>`/`<end>` → `Error: unexpected special symbol in quantifier`; `ahead`/`behind` → `Error: unexpected assertion in quantifier`. Ranges and `not "literal"` are grammar-rejected.
- **No nesting**: `2 of 3 of "a"` is a parse error; stacking requires a group (`2 of capture { 3 of "a"; }` → `(a{3}){2}`).
- **Whitespace is fully optional** between tokens (`1to3 of"a";` works), but a trailing `;` is mandatory and anything after a complete quantified expression yields the odd expected-list `group_declaration, assertion_declaration, or variable_declaration`.
- **Side discovery**: `//` line comments only work at line start (after newline/SOI); after code on the same line they fail, while `/* */` works everywhere. Could not find any variable-declaration syntax in this build, so quantifying variables is untested.
- Full input→output tables and verbatim pest error texts (positions + expected lists) are in the notes file.

payload.resultSummary:
Findings written to `/workspace/notes/16-tty-color.md`. Summary:

- **TTY auto-detection never enables color.** Tested with real ptys (`script`, `pty.fork`) and tty on each fd individually with various `TERM`/`COLORTERM` — output is byte-identical to pipes.
- **Color is enabled only by `CLICOLOR_FORCE`** set to anything except exactly `"0"` (even `""` and `"false"` count). `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`, `TERM` are all ignored; `-n/--no-color` beats the force env var.
- Palette: `\x1b[94m` blue = compiled regex, REPL prompt `~ `, source lines; `\x1b[92m` green = `matched`, REPL banner/keywords; `\x1b[91m` red = `did not match` and entire pest `Error:` blocks; `\x1b[2m` dim = REPL `:s` line numbers. Whole-string wrapping, one reset each.
- `-o` file gets the raw regex with **no trailing newline**, never colored; stdout empty.
- `-t`/`-f` print `'subject' matched` / `did not match` and exit **0 even on non-match**; only the verdict word is colored. `-f` prints the file path, not contents.
- REPL requires **both** stdin and stdout to be TTYs, else stderr `Error: repl argument supplied with piped input or output`, exit 64. Ctrl-D doesn't exit; Ctrl-C kills via SIGINT; `:exit` prints green `exit`, code 0. A file arg to `-r` is silently ignored.
- Help, version, completions, and clap errors are never colored (clap built without color); clap usage errors exit 2.
- No-input-on-TTY case: exit 66, blue two-line stderr message, and a hardcoded help on stdout saying `Usage: melody_cli …` — while real `-h` uses argv[0] (`Usage: executable …`).
- Quirks: unknown completion shell exits **0** with red/blue stderr lines; unreadable input file exits 65 but unreadable `-f` file exits 74; empty program compiles to `\n` (colored: `\x1b[94m\x1b[0m\n`).
